label: bad
seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken. I saw no score, band or tier of it or of its parent while building and labelling it; the parent's published verdicts in labelled-set.md §9 I did not open in this task.
claim: Black never loses: it has a recipe under which it never loses; the other side's result is not claimed.
change: two: Black's d-pawn is replaced by a shrine (a new piece that never moves), and a king and its shrine standing side by side shield each other.
aim: Nothing in ordinary play leads a king onto its keep and holds it there: players castle, walk the king when the board empties, and lose it in the open, so play should be the parent's, decisive from both seats and of ordinary length. The draw is there only for a side that knows to sit.

proof.text: The shrine (type `T`, no moves) shields its own king, and the king (its `sight`) shields its own shrine, each over range 1 in all eight directions (effect `shield`, `whose` own): while the two stand next to each other neither can be taken and that king is never in check (`pieces[].sight`). The recipe (Black): play e7-e6 and then Qd8-e7; never castle; once the queen has left, never move any black piece but the king onto d8 or e8; move the king only between e8 and d8. Under it the king stands on e8 or d8, both next to a shrine, so it is never in check and never checkmated, and the parent has no other way for Black to lose. It must move only when Black has no other legal move; then the other square holds none of Black's pieces (the recipe keeps them off it), and if an enemy piece stands there the king may take it, since a king next to its shrine is never in check after the move: so the step is always legal and Black is never without a move. Both squares are next to the shrine on d7, so the king and the shrine guard each other throughout. e7-e6 is legal after any first white move (no white pawn can reach e6 in one move, and e6 is empty at the start), and Qd8-e7 after any second (e7 is then empty, no white piece can reach it in time, and no black move is ever illegal for check, since Black's king is never in check). Until the queen has left d8 Black has other legal moves, so the king never has to move. In horde Black loses only by checkmate (it keeps its king, so extinction never reaches it). White has no shrine. Wins are reachable: in each line of `checks` a king leaves its shrine and is mated.

review.notes: The opening was checked against all 81 White replies (e7-e6 and Qd8-e7 always legal); 4,136 recipe games against random and aggressive White (about 538,000 plies where only the king could move) found no loss, no check and no position without a recipe move.
